correctness.rationale: The capped genus-two hyperelliptic monodromy acts on six Weierstrass points via σ∈S6 and on H1(Σ2;F2) via the even-subset quotient E/⟨1⟩ (dimension four). For a fibered knot the monodromy characteristic polynomial equals the Alexander polynomial up to a monomial; |ΔK(1)|=1 excludes eigenvalue 1 over F2. If σx=x+1 for an even representative x, all cycles must be even and alternating x would have exactly three 1s, impossible. Thus any fixed homology class is represented by a σ-invariant even union of cycles; no nontrivial even proper union forces precisely the partitions (6),(5,1),(3,3). Dividing the permutation-module characteristic polynomial ∏(t^ℓ−1) by (t−1)^2 yields t⁴+t³+t²+t+1 for (5,1) and t⁴+t²+1 for (6) and (3,3). Independent exhaustive F2 action on ALL 720 permutations (not reuse of saved log) returned precisely 120,144,40 zero-fixed classes, total 304. Knot-to-branch multisection correspondence relies on Akhmedov's hyperelliptic double-cover theorem, named as an imported premise; no claim that all three cycle types are realizable by knots.

originality.rationale: Resultary search using genus-two Weierstrass permutation, mod-two Alexander, orbit patterns and equivalent Sp(4,2) aliases returned no covering distinct theorem. Akhmedov arXiv:2610.00409 describes the genus-two branch locus components indexed by permutation orbits, while the submitted restriction additionally uses ΔK(1) parity to rule out all but three orbits and provides a mod-two Alexander discriminator. A separate Resultary paper on first homology of hyperelliptic branch complements uses arbitrary orbit lengths as inputs, without restricting the genus-two orbit partitions. Melvin–Morton 1986 discusses mod-two genus-two monodromy for Hopf plumbings, not a demonstrated implication of the complete branch-degree classification. Original Akhmedov full text and Melvin–Morton full primary text were not accessible in this run, so potential exact overlap remains an explicit material risk, not falsely dismissed as NOT_COVERING.
